latin: Corpus Christi ex se fuit impassibile.

mentions.context: basically what we have in Pico’s thesis, only that Pico uses the adverb subiective which is not found in Scotus. Thesis 12 states that the body of Christ was in itself incapable of suffering.58 This is discussed by Scotus in Ordinatio 4, d. 49, pars 2, q. unica, entitled: ‘whether the body of the blessed person after resurrection will be incapable of suffering’ (Utrum corpus hominis beati post resurrectionem erit impassibile).59
